title: Add support for snappy content encoding to http packet dissector
description:
Wireshark fails to decompress snappy encoded http content.

This patch is essentially based on `epan/tvbuff_brotli.c` and `epan/dissectors/packet-mongo.c`.

My motivation was to export Prometheus protobuf messages from the remote_write API to files, using tshark and the `--export-objects` functionality.

Adding support for snappy to the http packet dissector fixes this use case too.

Skimming through the code, it seems that data with an unsupported "content encoding" will not run through listening taps (see early `goto body_dissected` in `dissect_http_message()`).

In my case, I would have been fine with dumping the raw http body and uncompressing the data later on using an external tool.

I was therefore wondering if it would make to sense to enable that as well, in addition to this patch?

notes.body:
can you share a pcap with HTTP Snappy ?

Mongo dissector can't reuse the code ?

Here's a minimalist capture of a write request from Prometheus to a "remote_write" endpoint (both running on localhost.)
[prometheus-remote-write.pcapng](/uploads/2b0f9c760fc9c741f58033be13fb1fcf/prometheus-remote-write.pcapng)

The patch is more precisely "inspired" by tvbuff_brotli and mongo dissestor in the sense that they are simple examples of how to hook a decompressor (tvbuff_brotli) and how to call the snappy library API in the context of wireshark.
Regarding snappy, it is only a matter of calling a couple of functions so I'm not sure it would add much benefit to share code with mongo dissector.

There's four existing dissectors that do snappy decompression, I think it would be a benefit if they could all use the shared code. For example, anything that moves calls to `tvb_get_ptr()` to the library instead of a dissector body is welcome.
@johnthacker do you have time for make shared code ? or @dariusd0

This change appears to already implement reusable/shared code -- as long as it can be made to include the memory-allocation safety check I commented on in the other thread.

The other four dissectors supporting Snappy decompression (Couchbase, Kafka, Mongo and CQL) can be subsequently updated (in a separate change) to use this new shared code.

I've started a draft of a change to update the other four dissectors to use the `tvb_uncompress_snappy` functions supplied by this change, and I'm happy to roll in the addition of the safety check as part of my draft if you're otherwise happy for this merge request to be committed as-is.

The Mongo and CQL dissectors have a safety check here to prevent a malformed/malicious packet from attempting to allocate too much memory -- `orig_size` is limited to 20 MBytes for Mongo and 10 MBytes for CQL, and no attempt will be made to decompress larger inputs.  It would seem advisable to have something similar here, even if it is just a facility to allow the caller to supply a size limit.
